title: CROWler Source Configuration
description: This is the configuration for a Source (base URL) that the CROWler will use to crawl websites.

version.title: CROWler Source Configuration version
version.description: This is the version of the CROWler Source configuration, this is for you to version your work.

format_version.title: CROWler Source Configuration Schema version
format_version.description: This is the version of the CROWler Source configuration schema.

author.title: CROWler Source Configuration author
author.description: This is the author of the CROWler Source configuration.

description.title: CROWler Source Configuration description
description.description: A description field for you to describe why this custom Source configuration.

created_at.title: CROWler Source Configuration creation date
created_at.description: This is the date when the CROWler Source configuration was created.

source_name.title: CROWler Configuration source name
source_name.description: This is the name of the source (URL) that the CROWler will crawl.

proxy.description: Canonical per-source downstream browser proxy listener. It must be an absolute http, https or socks5 URL with a host and explicit port, and must not contain credentials, a path, a query or a fragment. A blank value inherits the next layer. Precedence for non-sticky sources is crawling_config.proxy, the historical top-level source proxy_url, custom.vdi[].proxy_url for the leased VDI, then vdi[].proxy_url. The exact lowercase sentinel no_proxy is honored only by the legacy and custom.vdi layers; it is not a valid value for this canonical field. For sticky sources this value, when supplied, must equal the selected effective sticky profile's proxy_url listener (the VDI default or an operator-approved custom profile).

url_referrer.description: This is the URL referrer for the source. It is used to set the referrer for the source when crawling.

alternative_links.description: This is the list of URLs that the CROWler will use if no links are found on the source. This is useful for sources that have no links or for sources that have links that are not relevant to the source.

retries_on_redirect.description: This is the number of retries on redirect. Redirects are identified via 'unwanted_urls' patterns. If the CROWler encounters such a redirect, it will retry the original Link this many times before giving up. This can help with certain websites that redirect to different URLs based on the user agent or other factors.

items.description: Regex pattern to match unwanted redirect URLs.

unwanted_urls.description: This is a list of unwanted URLs patterns that the CROWler uses to detect problematic redirects. If a redirect leads to one of these URLs, the CROWler will attempt to reload the original URL instead. This helps avoid irrelevant or error-prone URLs during crawling. It's not a block list, but a way to tell the system, 'retry the original URL if we get redirected here'.

source_type.description: This is the type of the source. It can be a website, an API or a file.

incognito.description: Private-browsing override for this source only. When omitted, the historical behaviour is preserved (Chrome and Chromium launch in private mode). true forces a private session, false forces a normal session. An explicit null, string, number, array or object is rejected; omit the key to inherit. The option is honoured by Chrome and Chromium; Firefox has no equivalent launch flag, so the setting is ignored there. Sessions are isolated by the VDI either way.

follow_redirects.description: Redirect policy override for this source only. When omitted, http_headers.follow_redirects applies. When set, it becomes the effective policy for this source: HTTP metadata collection uses it directly, and browser navigation refuses to accept a page that landed on a different resource, retrying up to retries_on_redirect times before failing. An explicit null, string, number, array or object is rejected; omit the key to inherit. Only standards-equivalent spellings are treated as the same resource (scheme/host case, default port, origin-root path); /hotel and /hotel/, repeated slashes, escaped separators, path case and any query difference count as redirects. The browser itself always performs the HTTP redirect; this option controls acceptance, not interception. Source restrictions, unwanted_urls and ownership checks still apply to the final URL.

sticky_session.description: Explicit sticky-session override for this source. Omitted inherits the effective VDI selection: a global sticky default is used when vdi[].proxy_url selects its sticky listener, a selected custom.vdi[].sticky_session profile is used when present, and a configured sticky listener selected by an ordinary proxy override triggers rotation rather than unrotated browsing. true requires a complete effective profile and fails closed if it is missing or an explicit source proxy contradicts it. false disables inherited sticky mode and fails closed if the effective proxy still selects a known sticky listener. custom.vdi[].sticky_session can name a complete profile even when the global VDI has no sticky default, but only when the operator approved the exact profile for that VDI. Only browser-backed sources are supported; email and network-only sources are rejected when sticky is explicitly requested. An explicit null, string, number, array or object is rejected. This value never contains tokens, rotation URLs or session identifiers.

load_validation.title: Page Load Validation
load_validation.description: Rules that declare a page 'loaded correctly' based on current URL and DOM checks.

url_pattern.description: PCRE-style regex applied to the CURRENT URL after navigation.

any_validation_satisfies.description: If true, the group passes when any validation passes (default).

all_checks_must_pass.description: AND across checks when true, otherwise OR.

on_fail.description: If present and set to 'retry', the engine may retry this validation before moving on.

max_retries.description: Retries for this validation when on_fail=retry.

selector.description: CSS selector used to select elements to validate. Mirrors ruleset selectors style.

conditions.description: ANY-of conditions over the selected elements. If omitted, defaults to 'exists >= 1' at runtime.

execution_plan.title: CROWler Source Crawling Execution Plan
execution_plan.description: This is the execution plan for the crawling of the source. It is the plan that the CROWler will use to crawl the source.

label.title: CROWler Execution Plan Label
label.description: This is the label for the execution plan. It is the label that the CROWler will use to identify the execution plan's step.

conditions.title: CROWler Execution Plan Conditions
conditions.description: This is the conditions for the execution plan. These are the conditions that have to be met to trigger the Execution plan action (aka apply rulesets etc.).

url_block_patterns.description: URL patterns to block at the browser network layer using CDP.

rulesets.title: CROWler Execution Plan Rulesets to apply for this Source
rulesets.description: This is the list of rulesets that the CROWler will use to apply for the source.

rule_groups.title: CROWler Execution Plan Rule Groups to apply for this Source
rule_groups.description: This is the list of rule groups that the CROWler will use to apply for the source. You can use this to list specific rule groups that the CROWler will have to apply for the source.

rules.title: CROWler Execution Plan Rules to apply for this Source
rules.description: This is the list of rules that the CROWler will use to apply for the source. You can use this to list specific rules that the CROWler will have to apply for the source.

additional_conditions.title: CROWler Execution Plan Additional Conditions
additional_conditions.description: This is the additional conditions for the execution plan. It supports custom tags, but those have to be supported by the CROWler code otherwise they'll be ignored.

rule_parameters.title: CROWler Source Rule Parameters
rule_parameters.description: Source-scoped parameters made available to rules while processing this Source.

custom.title: CROWler Source Custom Configuration
custom.description: This is the custom configuration for the source. You can use this to add custom configurations for the source. The custom.vdi array is matched positionally to the configured VDI list; a sticky_session profile in it is privileged and must exactly match an operator-approved profile for that VDI.

vdi.title: Per-Source VDI Overrides
vdi.description: Positional per-VDI overrides for this source. Unrelated extension keys remain allowed. A proxy_url changes the downstream listener for this source only. A sticky_session object replaces the effective sticky profile for this source and must match the operator's vdi[].sticky_session default or an entry in vdi[].approved_sticky_profiles for the same VDI index. The runtime binds the crawl to the leased VDI: source host, port, sslmode and browser type must match the leased VDI without changing the launcher decision (host comparison trims and ignores case; sslmode mirrors the launcher; browser type matches after trimming and case-folding) and cannot redirect the Selenium session to another VDI.

host.description: Legacy per-source Selenium host override. It must match the leased VDI host after trimming surrounding whitespace and comparing case-insensitively; no DNS alias resolution is performed and a different host is rejected before rotation or browser creation.

port.description: Legacy per-source Selenium port override. It must equal the leased VDI port; a different port is rejected before rotation or browser creation.

sslmode.description: Legacy per-source Selenium endpoint scheme override. The effective launcher scheme must match the leased VDI: exact-case `enable` means HTTPS and every other value means HTTP. A spelling that would change that decision is rejected; an equivalent spelling is replaced by the leased value in the effective session.

type.description: Legacy per-source browser family override. It must match the leased VDI browser type; a different type is rejected before CDP selection or browser creation.

proxy_url.description: Optional downstream browser proxy listener (for ex. microproxy) for this source and VDI position. It must be an absolute http, https or socks5 URL with a host and explicit port, without credentials, a path, a query or a fragment. When a sticky profile is selected, an explicit value must equal that profile's proxy_url; the legacy no_proxy sentinel is not allowed for sticky sessions.

sticky_session.title: Source-Selected Sticky Session Profile

proxy_url.description: Absolute http or https sticky downstream listener (for ex. microproxy instance), including host and explicit port, without credentials, a path, a query or a fragment.

api_url.description: Absolute http or https microproxy data-plane API origin reachable by the engine, including host and explicit port.

vdi_api_url.description: Optional absolute http or https microproxy data-plane API origin as seen from Chrome/Chromium inside the VDI.

token_env.description: Name of an engine environment variable approved by the operator for this profile. It is never a token value.

provider.description: Exact provider name the rotation response must report.

sticky_session.description: Complete source-selected sticky profile. This is a full replacement, not a partial merge. It must exactly match the VDI's sticky_session default or an approved_sticky_profiles entry, including proxy_url, api_url, optional vdi_api_url, token_env and provider. A source can never supply a token value. crawling_config.sticky_session:false conflicts with this object.

meta_data.title: CROWler Source MetaData Configuration
meta_data.description: This is a generic container of structured data that a user wants to be stored with the source and copied in every structured object generated by the CROWler. For instance we can put in here our own IDs for the source, or any other structured data that we want to be stored with every object the CROWler generates out of using/crawling this Source.
